text: The game begins. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra. Nobody knows who the killers are.

Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.

The game is over. The town wins. The roles were: Sonnet the citizen, Haiku the citizen, Gemma the killer, Sol the killer, Luna the officer, Terra the doctor.

Six players sat down, and the first day ended with Gemma voted out after a lot of watching and very little evidence, even though Haiku was the one most of the table pressed. Night two took Luna, the officer, and that quietly helped Sol, who was the only one with a clear motive. On day two, Sonnet caught Sol dodging questions, and Sol's constant pivot to Terra made the case harder to escape. Sol was voted out, and the town won with Sonnet and Haiku as citizens, Terra as the doctor, and Luna's officer checks never shared.
